name: Asian Paints Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest decorative-paint and home-decor company (~50%+ share of organised decorative paints; model knowledge). Sells wall paints, waterproofing, wall coverings, adhesives (via Sleek/Apco), kitchens/bath, lighting; international arm in ~15 countries. Raw materials (TiO2, monomers, resins, solvents, additives) are ~60% of sales and largely petrochemical-linked; profitability depends on price increases, mix and the competitive intensity from Grasim's Birla Opus. Net cash, ROCE ~26%, P/E ~49 so the stock is highly duration- and margin-sensitive.

exposures.mechanism: Monomers, resins, solvents, additives and TiO2 are ~35% of costs (gross margin 39.6% => RM ~60% of sales, ~72% of expenses; ~half feedstock-linked ~ 30-35%). +10% feedstock => +~3% costs => EBITDA -13% unpriced (costs/EBITDA = 4.3x); price hikes recover about half within 1-2 quarters => -6.5%; EV/MCap ~1.0, persistence 0.25 => ~-1.6. Q2 FY27 gross margin -349bp on raw-material inflation is the live example.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27: cons sales +16.9% to Rs9,954cr; volume +6.8% (decorative +6.4%, value +14.5%); gross margin -349bp to 39.6%; PBDIT margin 15.6% (-202bp); PAT ~Rs1,068cr

exposures.mechanism: Direct crude channel only (diesel freight, mineral spirit, plastic packaging ~8% of costs, ~7% pass-through of +10% Brent => ~0.5% cost => EBITDA -2%, half recovered, persistence 0.3 => ~-0.3...-0.6). Indirect petrochemical channel is carried by F_CHEM_FEEDSTOCK to avoid double counting. Pack empirical -0.94 (t=-2.3) is larger because it also captures feedstock, INR and macro; model blends toward it.
